buyer.name: LG Energy Solution in the US
buyer.summary: In US trade data LG Energy Solution appears mostly as a seller of cells. As a buyer, its storage unit LG Energy Solution Vertech takes cells from the Korean parent and from the group's plant in Nanjing, China. Ultium Cells, its venture with GM, received 53 rows of Chinese artificial graphite from Shanghai Shanshan in 2024-2025, and BTR graphite now reaches the Arizona plant and GM records that name LG Energy Solution. The Honda (L-H Battery) and Hyundai ventures showed no supplier rows in this scan.

scan.note: Sayari trade data checked on 18 Oct 2026 for HS 3801 (graphite, including anode material) and HS 8507 (batteries and parts) entering the US on rows that name 'LG Energy Solution' or 'LG Energy Solution Vertech'. Many graphite rows list General Motors as consignee and LG Energy Solution as notify party; they are counted as LG Energy Solution and Ultium supply, and each note says when the recorded buyer is GM. Facet counts ignored the 2024 date filter and are marked where used. The scan cannot see purchases inside the US, the L-H Battery (Honda) and Hyundai ventures under their own names, or the producer behind about 90 graphite rows with no named shipper (65 and 9 to GM, 2 to LG Energy Solution Arizona, 14 through OEC Freight). Shanghai Shanshan Tech is left out because its 14 rows are all from 2020-2022. Forwarders excluded: Xiamen Port Logistics (97 rows of cells from China to GM, 2026) and OEC Freight (NY) (consignee on 14 graphite rows).

calls.question: Who owns the Shanshan anode business that ships to Ultium Cells?
calls.result_summary: Ningbo Shanshan Co., Ltd. (Shanghai-listed, 600884) says on its own website that it runs anode production bases including Shanghai Shanshan. SMM lists 'Shanghai Shanshan New Materials' among Shanshan Technology's bases. GraphiteHub and BigGo report that the controlling Shanshan Group entered court restructuring in 2025, with BTR-led and Anhui state-capital investor groups bidding.
calls.interpretation: Shanghai Shanshan New Material is part of the Chinese Shanshan group. Its controlling shareholder is being restructured, possibly towards Chinese state-linked capital. This is not confirmed.

calls.question: Who owns LG Energy Solution, Ltd. and LG Chem?
calls.result_summary: LG Energy Solution is a subsidiary of LG Chem, Ltd. Its other shareholders are Korea's National Pension Service and an employee stock association. LG Chem's shareholders include LG Corp., the LG Yonam Foundation and the National Pension Service. One record also lists LG Chem (Chongqing) Engineering Plastics as an LG Chem shareholder, which looks like a data error.
calls.interpretation: Korean ownership through LG Chem and LG Corp. The Chongqing link is probably reversed (a subsidiary entered as a shareholder) and doesn't change the conclusion.
